manifest.name: Payment Provider: Demo
manifest.summary: A payment provider for running fake payment flows for demo purposes.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Payment Provider (Demo: code selection_add + all feature flags enabled + live-state constraint)
Payment Token (demo_simulated_state: per-token outcome selector for off-session charges)
Payment Transaction (capture_manually related + full simulation of all payment lifecycle hooks)

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security. Demo provider is permanently blocked from 'enabled' state by an @api.constrains check in payment_provider.py.

views.note: xml_loc=324: QWeb templates in payment_demo_templates.xml: inline_form (customer_input + simulated_payment_state dropdown), token_inline_form (shows outcome warning per demo_simulated_state), express_checkout_form (modal with submit button), express_inline_form (shipping fields), payment_details (shared input fragment). Also payment_provider_views.xml, payment_token_views.xml (demo_simulated_state on token form), payment_transaction_views.xml (manual capture action button). No own model list/kanban/graph views.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._compute_feature_support_fields + @api.constrains('state','code') -- Demo declares full feature support but is permanently blocked from going live
behavioral_notes.observation: payment_provider.py _compute_feature_support_fields forces support_express_checkout=True, support_manual_capture='partial', support_refund='partial', support_tokenization=True for code=='demo' -- the Demo provider announces every optional feature the payment engine can exercise, making it the canonical test bed for all payment flows. Simultaneously @api.constrains('state','code') raises UserError if the Demo provider's state is set to anything other than 'test' or 'disabled', making it impossible to activate it to 'enabled' (live). This safety rail lets Demo exercise all code paths in staging but can never process real payments even if an admin tries.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._apply_updates -- simulation hub: manual-capture split, refund self-triggering cron, and per-state dispatch
behavioral_notes.observation: _apply_updates (payment_transaction.py) is the core simulation dispatch. It sets provider_reference = f'demo-{self.reference}', optionally calls self._tokenize(payment_data) when self.tokenize is set, then dispatches on payment_data['simulated_state']: 'pending' -> _set_pending(); 'done' AND capture_manually AND NOT payment_data.get('manual_capture') -> _set_authorized() (two-step authorize-then-capture path); 'done' in all other cases -> _set_done(), and if self.operation=='refund' immediately fires env.ref('payment.cron_post_process_payment_tx')._trigger() to process the refund downstream without waiting for the next scheduled cron run; 'cancel' -> _set_canceled(); any other value -> _set_error(). The capture_manually two-step path and the inline cron trigger for refund post-processing are invisible to model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._send_payment_request -- off-session simulation reads token.demo_simulated_state for deterministic recurring-charge outcomes
behavioral_notes.observation: _send_payment_request (payment_transaction.py) overrides the engine's off-session hook: for code=='demo' it reads simulated_state = self.token_id.demo_simulated_state and immediately calls self._process('demo', {'reference': self.reference, 'simulated_state': simulated_state}). There is no HTTP call; the entire off-session payment lifecycle is driven by the per-token Selection field added to payment.token. A QA engineer can pre-configure a saved Demo token to always succeed, always fail, always stay pending, or always cancel -- enabling deterministic test coverage of subscription / auto-renewal code paths without any gateway account.

behavioral_notes.element: JS frontend (payment_demo_mixin.js + payment_form.js + express_checkout.js) -- browser reads dropdown, posts to simulate_payment, handles express checkout shipping modal
behavioral_notes.observation: payment_form.js patches PaymentForm._prepareInlineForm to force 'direct' flow for demo (bypassing redirect) and patches _processDirectFlow to delegate to paymentDemoMixin.processDemoPayment(). The mixin (payment_demo_mixin.js) reads customerInput and simulatedPaymentState from the DOM and calls rpc('/payment/demo/simulate_payment', {reference, payment_details, simulated_state}) then redirects to /payment/status. express_checkout.js patches ExpressCheckout.initiateExpressPayment to additionally collect shipping fields from a modal (name/email/street/street2/zip/city/country), call the shippingAddressUpdateRoute RPC to resolve delivery methods, set the first available delivery method via /shop/set_delivery_method, then call processDemoPayment -- exercising the full Express Checkout (Apple/Google Pay-equivalent) flow in software. These DOM-driven simulation mechanics are invisible to Python metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._extract_token_values -- tokenization stores simulated_state on payment.token; double-tokenization guard coordinates with _apply_updates
behavioral_notes.observation: _extract_token_values (payment_transaction.py) is called by the payment engine after a tokenize transaction. For 'demo' it returns {'payment_details': payment_data['payment_details'], 'provider_ref': 'fake provider reference', 'demo_simulated_state': state}. The customer_input text from the form becomes token.payment_details and the chosen simulated_payment_state becomes the permanent token.demo_simulated_state for future off-session charges. However, _apply_updates already calls self._tokenize(payment_data) inline in the 'done'/'authorized' branch. To prevent double-tokenization, _extract_token_values opens with 'if self.state in (done, authorized): return {}' -- a guard that only makes sense if you have read both methods and understand their sequencing.

external_integrations.auth: none -- no outbound HTTP; simulation is entirely in-process
external_integrations.pattern: Intentionally zero external integration: payment_demo exists to exercise the full Odoo payment engine in-process without any live gateway. All responses are synthesized from user-selected simulated_payment_state or from per-token demo_simulated_state. This is the canonical reference implementation and test harness for payment module development.

capabilities: Simulate a successful, pending, cancelled, or errored payment via the standard checkout form (user selects outcome from dropdown)
Simulate Express Checkout (Apple/Google Pay-equivalent) with shipping address collection and delivery method selection via modal
Simulate partial and full refunds with immediate cron post-processing trigger
Simulate tokenization / saved-payment-method creation with configurable off-session outcomes (demo_simulated_state on token)
Simulate off-session recurring / subscription charges using per-token outcome selector
Enforce that Demo can never be set to 'enabled' (live) state -- UserError constraint in _check_provider_state
value_streams: Demo-Checkout: user selects demo payment -> PaymentForm forces 'direct' flow -> inline form (customer_input + outcome dropdown) -> paymentDemoMixin rpc /payment/demo/simulate_payment -> _process('demo') -> _apply_updates -> state machine -> /payment/status
Demo-ExpressCheckout: ExpressCheckout modal collects shipping -> sets delivery method via RPC -> processDemoPayment -> same simulation path as above
Demo-Tokenize: checkout with tokenize=True -> _apply_updates calls _tokenize inline -> payment.token created with demo_simulated_state + payment_details from customer_input
Demo-OffSession: engine calls _send_payment_request -> reads token.demo_simulated_state -> _process in-process (no HTTP) -> state machine (subscription / auto-payment test path)
Demo-ManualCapture: checkout with capture_manually provider -> _apply_updates -> _set_authorized(); then action_demo_set_done -> _process with manual_capture=True -> _set_done()
Demo-Refund: engine calls _send_refund_request -> simulates done -> _apply_updates + operation=='refund' -> _set_done + immediate cron trigger for downstream account entries
information_concepts: payment.provider (Demo configuration: code='demo', all feature flags, blocked from live state)
payment.token (saved demo payment method: demo_simulated_state controls future off-session outcome)
payment.transaction (simulation record: simulated_state drives the lifecycle; provider_reference='demo-{reference}')
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; inherits payment's groups; no API credentials required)
policies: Demo provider MUST NOT be set to 'enabled': @api.constrains('state','code') raises UserError if state not in ('test','disabled') for code=='demo'
All four simulated outcomes (pending/done/cancel/error) available via simulated_payment_state dropdown -- QA can force any branch
Manual capture: _apply_updates withholds _set_done() and calls _set_authorized() when capture_manually=True and manual_capture flag is absent
Refund post-processing: a completed refund simulation immediately self-triggers the post-process cron so downstream effects complete without waiting for the scheduler
Double-tokenization prevention: _extract_token_values returns {} if tx already in done/authorized state (because _apply_updates already tokenized inline)

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments; payment testing infrastructure)
classification.rationale: payment_demo is classified value-NETWORK following the same Stabell & Fjeldstad logic as all payment acquirer adapters: its structural role is to mediate between payer and merchant within the payment engine's network topology. Unlike a real acquirer it makes no outbound connections -- all simulation is in-process -- but it is still classified 'network' because (a) it inherits the payment engine's network position, (b) it exists to test the full network-mediating behavior of real acquirers, and (c) its value is in mediation simulation rather than data transformation (chain) or bespoke problem-solving (shop). activity_class='support': payment infrastructure is a support function under APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources, and Demo specifically is development/QA support infrastructure with application=False.

typical_fits: developer testing of all payment engine flows (direct/redirect/token/refund/capture/express) without a live gateway account

onboarding new payment module developers by showing how all payment engine hooks should be overridden

not suitable for load/performance testing of payment flows
